intervention.title: Repair gaps between tests and real use
intervention.summary: Audit where existing tests bypass connections that users rely on, then change the project’s test setup and QA instructions to cover those gaps on relevant future work.

purpose.p: Make the software factory test the behavior it claims to have checked. The repository’s tests and the instructions for choosing them are part of that factory; adding an isolated test without changing future verification can leave the same mistake in place.

precondition.title: A gap in existing verification
precondition.p: Unsupported verification claims or component checks mistaken for complete verification point to a gap: individual parts pass, but their connection is untested. A confirmed diagnosis is not required to repair a demonstrated coverage gap.

precondition.title: Access to the test setup
precondition.p: You can change the project’s test setup and QA guidance, and exercise the relevant behavior within the user’s access, cost, and safety limits.

step.title: Find what the tests skip
step.p: Take a recent claim that a feature works and inspect the tests behind it. Compare the user’s steps with the test’s steps. Look for mocked services, directly called handlers, skipped serialization, or deployment differences that hide a connection the user depends on.

step.title: Choose the useful checks
step.p: Review the consequential gaps with the user or maintainer. Select the smallest tests that exercise those connections; keep fast component tests for the problems they already catch.

step.title: Exercise the missing connections
step.p: Repair the test setup and fixtures so those checks use the relevant interfaces. For a keyboard feature, send a keypress through the UI rather than calling the handler directly. Use a safe test environment for workflows with external effects.

step.title: Change the recurring QA workflow
step.p: Update the QA skill, project instructions, and relevant CI job so agents routinely choose the repaired checks when that behavior changes. Remove any rule that treats a component pass as proof that the entire workflow works.

step.title: Review later work
step.p: At an agreed check-in, inspect a few ordinary changes involving those connections. Check whether the intended tests ran, what they found, and whether the final report describes the evidence accurately.

ul.li: Expect previously hidden integration bugs to become visible. Finding them can be progress even before the code has been repaired.
Check that unsupported verification claims decline because relevant testing improved. A cautious final answer with the same missing coverage is only a reporting improvement.
Component-only work should remain cheap. If every change now triggers a large end-to-end suite, narrow the selection rule.
Broader tests can be slow, flaky, or affect external systems. Match them to the actual task and use an authorized test environment.
A new test may share the implementation’s mistaken assumptions. Compare its steps with real use, not just the code it tests.
Narrow or revert a check that introduces unauthorized effects, false failures, or disproportionate delay.
Keep any removed coverage marked as untested until a suitable replacement exists.
